editorial_underclaims.original_statement: A preadditive category with countable products and kernels of all split epimorphisms is Karoubian; dually for coproducts and split monomorphisms.
editorial_underclaims.proved_statement: For a fixed X and idempotent e, existence of the countable power X^N and of the kernel of the explicitly displayed split epimorphism Phi suffices to construct ker(e), via its first coordinate. Thus countable powers, rather than all countable products, suffice for the original global conclusion when the required kernels exist for every X and e.
editorial_underclaims.caveat: For the decomposition of a particular object into both summands, apply the argument to both e and 1-e. A kernel of e alone is not asserted to supply both summands.
editorial_underclaims.propagation_status: receiving_use_checked; no existing conclusion invalidated; separate supplement pending

editorial_underclaims.original_statement: An additive retraction b with right adjoint a, abelian source, left exact b, and ba naturally isomorphic to the identity gives an abelian target.
editorial_underclaims.proved_statement: Let A be preadditive, B abelian, b:B->A additive and preserving kernel and cokernel diagrams, a:A->B a functor, and theta:ba->Id_A a natural isomorphism. Then A is abelian, with the exact transported zero, biproduct, kernel, cokernel and canonical coimage-to-image maps in the proof.
editorial_underclaims.propagation_status: receiving_use_checked; original adjunction supplies the preservation hypotheses; separate supplement pending

editorial_underclaims.original_statement: The kernel of K_0(C)->K_0(A) consists of the differences [H^0]-[H^1] of the specified periodic complexes exact in A/C.
editorial_underclaims.proved_statement: For prescribed objects P,Q of a small abelian category A, [P]=[Q] in K_0(A) if and only if there is a periodic complex on one object M whose H^0 is isomorphic to P and whose H^1 is isomorphic to Q. If P,Q lie in a Serre subcategory C, the constructed complex is exact in A/C.
editorial_underclaims.exact_transport: Use the labelled permutation J:M^+->M^- and the source maps phi:M^+->M^-, psi:M^-->M^+. On M=M^+ set phi_hat=psi J and psi_hat=J^{-1} phi. All summands, zero components and signs are retained.

editorial_underclaims.original_statement: A left dual implies finite total dimension and nondegenerate opposite-degree pairings.
editorial_underclaims.proved_statement: A graded F-vector space has a left dual if and only if its total dimension is finite; evaluation identifies W^{-n} with (V^n)^*. The displayed finite coevaluation and evaluation obey both triangles and are basis-independent.
affected_results: Weil graded-dual uses at current-source lines 1723, 2888, 4646, 4717

editorial_underclaims.original_statement: For a morphism between finite filtered objects, strictness, graded coimage-image isomorphism and either exactness condition at gr(A) or gr(B) are equivalent.
editorial_underclaims.proved_statement: On I=im(f), put P^p=f(F^p A), Q^p=I intersect F^p B. If P^m=I, monicity of gr(P)->gr(Q) forces strictness. If Q^n=0, epicity forces strictness. Both bounds give all six original equivalences without requiring finite filtrations on the full source and target.
corollaries: Finite source filtration alone suffices for gr(f) monic iff f is a strict monomorphism.
Finite target filtration alone suffices for gr(f) epic iff f is a strict epimorphism.
editorial_underclaims.exact_maps: The underlying identity c:(I,P)->(I,Q) is the canonical coimage-image map transported via A/ker(f) -> I. Its graded kernel and image are the explicit subquotients in proof equations (3.1).
editorial_underclaims.counterexamples: Three explicit identity maps on a nonzero vector space show failures without the correct bound/direction.
affected_results: Derived filtration uses at the nine recorded lines
editorial_underclaims.propagation: Original finite applications remain valid; weaker criteria recorded separately. No wholesale generalization of the filtered derived category or surrounding exercises.
editorial_underclaims.next: Carry the exact image-filtration criteria and corollaries into the separate Homology editorial supplement.

editorial_underclaims.original_statement: The first differential is the connecting map of successive filtration quotients; if d raises filtration, it is induced directly by d. The statement additionally assumes countable direct sums.
editorial_underclaims.proved_statement: Both conclusions hold for every filtered complex in any abelian category; countable direct sums are unnecessary.
editorial_underclaims.hypotheses: A is abelian; F is decreasing and d preserves it. For the second assertion, d(F^p K^n) is contained in F^{p+1}K^{n+1} for all p,n.
editorial_underclaims.exact_maps: The short exact sequence gr^{p+1}K -> F^pK/F^{p+2}K -> gr^pK has connecting map [z] -> [d^n z], of bidegree (1,0), without any cochain translation.
editorial_underclaims.example: Finite-dimensional vector spaces give an abelian category without countable coproducts; the representative proof still applies.
editorial_underclaims.propagation: Bounded receiving applications checked; no source formula changes or unrelated removal of hypotheses. The editorial supplement carries the stronger statement and exact maps.

editorial_underclaims.proved_statement: Uniform acyclic upper tails and uniform quasi-isomorphic lower tails give the explicit finite filtered representative F^aK/F^bK through a zigzag of quasi-isomorphisms on every filtration step and every associated graded complex.
editorial_underclaims.hypotheses: Integers a<b work simultaneously in every cohomological degree; the source's merely degree-dependent bounds are not asserted to supply these uniform integers.
editorial_underclaims.propagation: Apply to the two K-flat resolutions to repair the existing existential Kunneth proof while preserving its bounded E0 conclusion and original E1 formula.

editorial_underclaims.proved_statement: The displayed totalization homotopy equivalence works in any additive category with the diagonal coproducts used by Tot; no abelian structure or exactness of coproducts is needed.
editorial_underclaims.hypotheses: The original outer homotopy equivalence and existence of its diagonal coproducts.
editorial_underclaims.propagation: Original abelian uses retain their convention that Tot exists. An explicit finite-dimensional counterexample shows outer contractibility does not force that existence.

editorial_underclaims.original_statement: The source assumes the ambient additive category is Karoubian to separate the two colimits and the two essentially constant summands.
editorial_underclaims.proved_statement: Given W=colim(F direct-sum G), colim F exists exactly when the induced F-projection idempotent e on W splits, and colim G exists exactly when 1-e splits. When the sum diagram is essentially constant, the corresponding splitting also gives an explicit essential-constancy witness for that summand.
editorial_underclaims.hypotheses: The specified sum colimit exists in the original additive category; each individual splitting is proved equivalent to its own colimit. No splitting of the complementary idempotent is inferred without proof.
editorial_underclaims.propagation: The receiving derived-functor proof supplies both splittings through its stated Karoubian hypothesis. The criterion isolates the requirement at its colimit value without changing its source statement or certifying its separate cofinality proof.

editorial_underclaims.original_statement: Acyclic complexes with matching maps surjective in every degree have acyclic ordinal inverse limit.
editorial_underclaims.proved_statement: For a fixed integer N, vanishing of H^q(K_beta) for q<=N and surjectivity of K_beta^j to lim_(gamma<beta) K_gamma^j for j<=N-2 imply H^q(lim K_beta)=0 for q<=N.
editorial_underclaims.hypotheses: An inverse system of complexes of abelian groups over a set-sized ordinal, with exactly the displayed degree ranges at every index.
editorial_underclaims.propagation: The all-degree assertion follows by applying the proved statement for every N. Existing Injectives and SDGA citations retain their original Homology conclusion; a degree-range refinement of their separate theorems has not been claimed.
